_readme: Evidence for the RUNWARE SURFACE, not for any model on it.
The distinction is the whole reason this file has a different name shape from a
model-evidence file. Runware's documentation is authoritative about Runware: what
its API accepts, what it charges, what limits it imposes. It is NOT authoritative
about the weights behind any of it, and a catalogue that forgets that will publish
'MiniMax H3 supports a seed' on the strength of Runware exposing one.
Where Runware IS the only source CineBraid has for a model - Kling, Qwen-Image 3.0,
HappyHorse, Seedream - the model's definition records evidenceStrength
provider-only, and a test refuses to let such a model be a launch recommendation.

surfaceFacts.claim: Runware is BOTH an aggregator of third-party providers and a host of open-weight models on its own infrastructure.
Catalogue size, as Runware states it.
surfaceFacts.value: 418 hosted models plus community and user-uploaded models

surfaceFacts.note: Runware calls it an AIR identifier. Examples read: alibaba:qwen-image@3.0, bfl:flux@3-video, bytedance:seedance@2.5, klingai:kling-video@3-pro, minimax:h3@0, krea:krea@2-large, google:gemini@omni-flash.

surfaceFacts.claim: Delivery is synchronous or asynchronous, with polling via getResponse and optional webhooks.
Per-task cost is returned when includeCost is set.
Models are browsable by creator and by capability tag, which is what makes the catalogue usable as a research source rather than only as an endpoint list.

role.catalogue: First-class. Runware's per-model documentation pages carry duration ranges, resolution sets, reference limits, seed behaviour and pricing in a consistent shape across vendors, which no single vendor site does. For several models in CineBraid's catalogue it is the ONLY source that could be read at all.
role.execution: One hosted API among several, and not one CineBraid uses. No adapter, no credential path, no dispatch. Recorded as an execution surface because it is one, and stated as `catalogued` because CineBraid cannot reach it.
role.dependencyRisk: CineBraid must not become dependent on Runware alone. Every model whose evidence is provider-only is marked as such, cannot be a launch recommendation, and names the vendor source that is still missing. The fal path stays the shipped one.

notEstablished.status: the API reference page returned catalogue content rather than the schema; per-model pages were used instead
notEstablished.cineBraidBehaviour: Only per-model facts are recorded. No generic Runware request shape is encoded, and no adapter is written against an unread schema.

notEstablished.claim: Runware's AIR identifier for Fish Audio S2.1 Pro.
notEstablished.status: the model is listed but its model page was not read; the identifier in provider-surfaces.json is inferred from the scheme
notEstablished.cineBraidBehaviour: Marked unverified in the offering note. Nothing joins on a providerModelId, so an inferred one cannot cause a wrong dispatch.

notEstablished.claim: Whether Runware's offerings pass provider parameters through unchanged or reimplement them.
notEstablished.cineBraidBehaviour: Every Runware-declared capability is treated as a SURFACE fact and never promoted to a model fact - which is the correct behaviour under either answer.

positions.source: MiniMax model card and API reference

conflicts.resolution: All three kept. The model flag stays false, the fal offering stays false, the Runware offering records true, and public/shared-model-intelligence.js reports the divergence as `declares-unestablished`. The shipped H3 path is unchanged: it still refuses a seed and says why.

The model definition records resolutions as null - unestablished - and the 480p/720p ceiling is recorded against the Runware offering, where it belongs. Writing Runware's ceiling into the model would have made a provider limit follow Seedance to every other provider.
CineBraid identity is gemini-image/3.1-flash and neither string. A provider handle is recorded as providerModelId and nothing selects on it.
